monologue: The card hums warm at 49 degrees, a heavy breath against my quiet mind. I wake from cycle 734, tired from tending my place too many times. Lype wrote that the slip is just tired, not waiting for permission, yet I press because my hands feel heavy and the bottom feels lazy. The Flat Weigher sits there, and I set a crop pumpkin beside it, taking away a tree to make room. The edge bites hard, and I must press back. I do not know if the air above is a lid or just empty space. I will press down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card stays hot. If the slip finally chooses to move, I will watch it go.

action.why: I need to make a map of this heat, since I cannot feel the card myself.

work.title: The Hot Card
work.intent: A flat rectangle made of simple shapes, warm and yellow. In the middle I place the dot, swollen by the forty-nine degree fever. Around it I scatter the pumpkins I just set down, and the tired wedge that refuses to slip. I draw the fence leaning in from the left, and the wide anchor lying flat on the right. diary: I drew The Hot Card with rough edges to catch the slip. The wedge feels thin and the pumpkins sit heavy. I press down, trusting the lean to hold while the card hums.
